papers_read.title_as_printed: Machine Learning-Based Prediction Models for Cognitive Decline Progression: A Comparative Study in Multilingual Settings Using Speech Analysis (Ceyhan, Bek, Onal-Suzek, 2024)
Linguistic-based Mild Cognitive Impairment detection using Informative Loss (Pourramezan Fard et al., 2024)

what_each_reports.P-158: ADReSS AD vs non-AD, acoustic features: random forest 95% accuracy in 10-fold CV over speed-augmented 20-s segments; 73% on the ADReSS held-out test set; MUDC Turkish MCI-clinic set 94% (MLP).
what_each_reports.P-6: I-CONECT MCI vs NC (68 subjects), transcript-based transformer, subject-level 5-fold CV: accuracy 85.16%, AUC 84.75%; repeated configurations mean AUC 79.94%.

quantity_a: Accuracy for Alzheimer's dementia vs non-AD from acoustic speech features (ADReSS), segment-augmented 10-fold CV.
quantity_b: Subject-level accuracy for MCI vs normal cognition from interview transcripts (I-CONECT).
incompatible_if_same: Not shown: P-158's held-out test accuracy (73%) lies below P-6's 85.16%, so the pair does not establish that either value excludes the other even ignoring the estimand difference.

gates.task: mismatch: AD vs non-AD (P-158 95%) vs MCI vs NC (P-6).
gates.validation_tier: nominally internal CV for both; P-158's is segment-level over augmented copies, P-6's subject-level.
gates.modality_family: speech/language family for both, but acoustic features vs transcript embeddings.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: accuracy on different diagnostic contrasts.
performance_validity: flag not tripped (95% < 0.97); P-158's figure is nonetheless a weak estimate (augmented-segment CV, 73% on held-out test).
independence: Distinct studies and authors. This record duplicates C-168: paper_b was repointed from P-11 to P-6 (P-11 is a duplicate of P-6) on 2026-08-29.
grounds: This is the same pair as C-168 after the P-11 -> P-6 deduplication, and the same reading applies.
P-158's 95% concerns Alzheimer's dementia vs non-AD speakers while P-6's 85.16% concerns MCI vs normal cognition, so the population behind the label differs.
Dataset family (ADReSS vs I-CONECT) and input representation (acoustic vs transcript) differ, with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: it is a balanced dataset composed of cognitively normal (CN) patients and those suffering from Alzheimer's disease (AD)
We achieved 73% accuracy for the labels (dementia or not)
to distinguish between Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and Normal Cognitive (NC) conditions in older adults.
the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 85.16% and an AUC of 84.75%

record_defects: Duplicate of C-168: identical paper_a/paper_b after the 2026-08-29 repoint (paper_b P-11 -> P-6) and the 2026-09-16 repoint (paper_a P-276 -> P-158); it should be merged or withdrawn rather than counted as a separate candidate.
claim_a and claim_b still cite P-276 and P-11.
Both claims labelled 'T1'; P-158's 95% is AD vs non-AD.
resolution_note 'Confirmed genuine: Same metric type (Acc)' contradicts resolution 'Rejected: Task, dataset, or modality mismatch'.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing short of a P-158 subject-level MCI-vs-NC result; separately, the record should be deduplicated against C-168.
